description: Make a private draft table, ready to fill, for anything from a tracker to a dataset. Its values say where they came from unless you set `proof` to `required`. Only `title`, `columns` and `rows` are needed now, but give `question`, `scope`, and a `rule` for each column if you can: a person has to supply them before publishing. Returns the column ids fill_cells needs, and the sheet's link, so tell your person to open it and watch it fill. Needs a token.

columns.description: Needed unless you use a template

choices.description: For a text column, the only values it takes, like a status list. An AI column answers with one of them

instruction.description: Makes it an AI column: what to work out for each row, naming other columns in braces, like "Classify {Pitch} by genre". Needs proof to be optional

rule.description: What counts as this value, so two readers would fill it in the same way

owner.description: A team you're on. Leave out for your own account

proof.description: `optional` (the default): each value says where it came from, like a person, a file, an email or a page. `required`: every value must quote a source word for word, for a table of public facts

rows.description: Row names. To add rows with their values, use add_rows after

scope.description: What belongs in the table and what doesn't

template.description: Start from a template, with its columns set up: `job-tracker` (Every application, where it stands and what's next, kept current from your email), `text-dataset` (Labeled examples to train or test a classifier, ready to load in a notebook), `reading-list` (What you want to read, what you're reading, and what you thought), `research-notes` (Sources and what each one says, with a topic your agent fills in). Then only `title` is optional

title.description: Needed unless you use a template

topic.description: A broad subject, like Law or Consumer tech

name: create_table
